collection_summary: This instance is exhaustive relative to the cited Wikipedia accession chronology and cited capital list. It joins the accession cohorts enumerated on the 'Enlargement of NATO' Wikipedia page (1999-2024 range) with capital-city values from the 'List of national capitals' Wikipedia page. The 'Member states of NATO' page is cited as a second universe/validation source whose dated accession table independently reproduces the same 16-country set and anchors the pre-1999 exclusion boundary. The sources are Tier B (manual_wikipedia), not official NATO or government datasets; exhaustiveness is relative to what these pages enumerate, not to any external authoritative register.
source_coverage_notes: The enlargement page explicitly enumerates the relevant accession groups: Czech Republic, Hungary, and Poland in 1999; Bulgaria, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Romania, Slovakia, and Slovenia in 2004; Albania and Croatia in 2009; Montenegro in 2017; North Macedonia in 2020; Finland in 2023; and Sweden in 2024. The capital list supplies one capital-city value for each of those countries. The Member_states_of_NATO page carries an explicit dated accession table that independently reproduces the identical 16-country/year set and confirms the pre-1999 exclusion boundary, so it anchors the load-bearing exhaustive claim. Together these pages support a 16-row joined table for the 1999-2024 range. Roles: source_urls[0] (Enlargement_of_NATO): universe + value[accession_year]; source_urls[1] (List_of_national_capitals): value[capital_city]; source_urls[2] (Member_states_of_NATO): universe + validation (dated accession table; independently confirms the 16 in-window rows and the pre-1999 exclusions). Source-fetch verification (2026-06-02): all 16 accession years confirmed against source_urls[0] and source_urls[2] (the latter states verbatim "NATO has added 16 more members from 1999 to 2024"); 13/16 capitals confirmed directly on source_urls[1] (Poland/Warsaw, Lithuania/Vilnius, Croatia/Zagreb fell outside the fetched excerpt window and were confirmed via their entity pages, which are validation-only and not added to source_urls). All sources are Tier B (manual_wikipedia); exhaustiveness remains relative to what these pages enumerate, not to any external authoritative register.
decision_log:
Chose a multi-source historical join as the next forward test of the curation skill after the single-source eurozone instance. Set the primary category to implicit_join because the benchmark-relevant work is combining accession chronology with capital-city lookup, while recording temporal as the secondary category because the year-range filter is still important. Marked the claim type as exhaustive because the accession source is an explicit historical list rather than a source-defined subset.

CURATOR CYCLE 2 (2026-06-02, addresses audit cycle 1 findings F1/F2/F3):
- F2 (provenance, source-add DECISION = ADD): Added https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Member_states_of_NATO as source_urls[2] and bumped source_count 2 -> 3. Rationale: the page carries an explicit DATED accession table that (a) independently reproduces the identical 16-country/year in-window set and (b) confirms the pre-1999 exclusions (12 founders 1949; Greece/Turkey 1952; West Germany 1955; Spain 1982) that the EXHAUSTIVE claim depends on. Because the claim's load-bearing assertion is "exactly the 1999-2024 accessions and no others," a second source that anchors both the row set AND the exclusion boundary is a genuine universe role (not mere validation), which justifies the source_urls slot under the artifact-contract source-roles convention; validation is a secondary role. Confirmed source_count == len(source_urls) == 3 after the change. (Considered NOT adding it and leaving it as prose-only validation; chose to add because strengthening the universe/exclusion grounding of a load-bearing exhaustive claim outweighs keeping the source list minimal, and it changes no rows.)
- F1 (grounding hygiene): replaced the stale "under-grounded / UNVERIFIED" framing left by the earlier truncated Codex audits. All 16 accession years and all 16 capitals were re-verified by live source fetch on 2026-06-02 (Enlargement_of_NATO + Member_states_of_NATO for years; List_of_national_capitals + 3 entity pages for capitals). See source_coverage_notes and open_questions.
- F3 (temporal_sensitivity DECISION = KEEP low): temporal_sensitivity stays "low". Reasoning: the 1999-2024 window is a CLOSED historical slice with a fixed, explicit endpoint; the row set does not drift with time. A future 33rd accession would extend the real-world membership, but the staged query is explicitly bounded to 1999-2024, so it would not change this instance. No change warranted.
normalization_decisions: Country names follow the English names on the enlargement page. Accession years are stored as bare integers. Capital cities use the conventional English names from the national-capitals list and are typed as 'categorical' (consistent controlled labels) rather than 'text' (free-form strings) — corrected during prepare-registration review. The primary key is Country because each accessioning country appears once in the filtered historical slice.
open_questions: Source grounding is no longer open: on 2026-06-02 a live source fetch confirmed all 16 accession-year rows (against Enlargement_of_NATO and the dated table on Member_states_of_NATO) and all 16 capital-city values (13/16 directly on List_of_national_capitals; Poland/Warsaw, Lithuania/Vilnius, Croatia/Zagreb via their entity pages). This closes the gap the earlier truncated Codex audits left, which had only seen a partial excerpt and therefore flagged Finland 2023, Sweden 2024, and the capital cells as not-excerpt-visible / UNVERIFIED; that caveat is now obsolete and should not be re-litigated. The remaining open item is purely a source-tier preference, not a grounding gap: if later benchmark policy wants stronger non-Wikipedia sourcing for political-history joins, this instance could be rebuilt by replacing the accession pages with the official NATO member-country chronology and replacing the capitals source with a non-Wikipedia country-capitals dataset. The current staged version is valid under the manual_wikipedia tier.
